physical_mismatches.reason: The original model is a 3D detailed thermal model of a molded eQFN package (die, die attach, epad, pins, mold, board). A 2D chip-level Studio placement cannot reproduce the vertical heat paths through the die attach, epad and board.

The paper uses JEDEC-style boundary conditions for the junction-to-ambient environment, with a board modelled as one parallelepiped of adjusted conductivity and pins as a homogenised block. Section 4.4 does not state the ambient or cooling boundary conditions for this case, so Studio cooling cannot be matched.

The solver differs. The paper uses a parametric projection-based compact model validated against FloTHERM finite-volume results, while Studio uses its own solver, so numerical results are not directly comparable.
The eQFN package has no interposer or 3D stacking, so those mismatches are not applicable, but the package-level geometry is not equivalent to a chiplet or interposer layout.

The paper has no optimizer, controller, reliability analysis or transient behaviour in this scenario (static case). Studio's optimizer or controller features therefore have no counterpart in the original setup.

studio_assumptions: No complete paper-derived floorplan can be built because the heat-source positions are available only in a figure sketch. Any Studio run would use a separate, illustrative 2D placement whose coordinates are generated by the runner and are not paper facts.

If an illustrative case is built, the published dimensions are the 4 x 4 mm2 die and four 1 x 1 mm2 sources, with 0.5 W each (2 W total, stated explicitly in the paper). No power is split by an unpublished rule.

Studio's bundled package and material assumptions would replace the paper's STMicroelectronics eQFN materials, pin and board homogenisation, and JEDEC boundary conditions. Temperatures from such a run must not be compared numerically with Table 1.
